stem:
Komal learns that in sexual reproduction each gamete carries half of a parent's genetic material. A male gamete and a female gamete join at fertilisation.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Joining two half-material gametes restores a complete mix of genetic information without doubling it each generation.
Each parent passes a complete set into every gamete, so joining two gametes doubles the genetic material.
Fertilisation happens first and that produces half-material gametes.
Sexual reproduction uses only one parent's gamete, so mixing never occurs.

teacher.key_rationale: Half-material gametes join to restore a full mixed set without doubling each generation. Dropping the half step predicts doubling. Fertilisation follows gamete formation, not the reverse. Two parents' gametes are required for the mix.
